With Neural Rendering on, it grades the picture NR returns, so the model never sees it and exposure, skin detection and reuse are not affected. With NR before Super Resolution the grade is applied before the upscaler; in Finished Picture mode it grades the finished picture, UI included (D3D12; Vulkan does not run that mode). With NR off, it grades the OptiScaler upscaler's output, before the game draws its HUD (needs an OptiScaler upscaler).
Add LUT adds another after the last one, up to four. They are applied top to bottom (the tick box switches a layer off and on and keeps its settings, the arrows move it, x removes it); each strength blends that layer only. Strong grades stack up.
Look input: a LUT made for a camera log space (ARRILogC4AWG4-to-..., S-Log3, ...) needs the picture in that space. Auto reads it from the file's header or name and converts the game's picture for it, so no conversion LUT is needed in front; an ordinary LUT gets the picture as it is. Exact on Linear HDR games, up to paper white on PQ, highlights estimated on SDR. Pick one by hand if Auto guesses wrong; None always uses the picture.

Leave as they are: NR works on the main picture only; the others stay as DLSS made them.
A model of their own: each gets its own model and history (more GPU time and video memory). It uses the main picture's exposure and scene cuts, and Superior Scaling, Reuse detail and the edit cache stand aside for it.
Share the main model: the old behaviour. The pictures take turns in one history, which mixes them and, before SR, can rebuild the model on every call (a freeze).

ui.auto.9f951a3bdf4a.text:
Below 100% Model resolution, how NR's result is enlarged.
Classic: the whole output.
Matched residual: only NR's changes; less blur and colour shift.
NVIDIA residual: only the changes, NVIDIA's way; with Upscale Method Bilinear, also kept on their side of edges.
Superior Scaling: its own Area downsample, frequency shaping and a private DLSS that steadies NR over time, including at 100% with Compress screen edges. Needs DirectX 12 and NVIDIA DLSS; where it cannot run, Matched residual is used. At 100% and above, the ordinary modes use the original Classic composition; a saved residual choice returns when Model resolution is reduced.

XeFG (Intel library): Intel's own XeFG makes the frames, F5Low paces them, up to 6x (unlocked in memory). Needs libxess_fg.dll and libxell.dll in OptiScaler's folder. A change here takes effect after a restart.

DLSS-G: NVIDIA's frame generation through a Streamline copy of its own, started with the game. A change here takes effect after a restart.

ui.auto.0aa9bc617fa8.text:
What makes the generated frames in F5Low

On every start f5low.dll builds this generator from libxess_fg.dll in memory, in the background (about half a second); it starts by itself when ready. Nothing is written to disk.
If it can't, it hands over to Intel's XeFG (up to 4x).
A change here takes effect after a restart.
